A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MLE-bench study and complete Appendices A.1-A.8. Text comparison and rendering checks support reliable comparison: 25 of 27 pages are visually identical, with differences confined to the version stamp and page 4.

before.justification: Sections 3-4 report original agent evaluations, resource-scaling experiments, and contamination analyses. Appendices A.3-A.4 report original rule-compliance and plagiarism analyses.

after.justification: Sections 3-4 and Appendices A.3-A.4 retain these original empirical results, including model and scaffold comparisons in Table 2.

M1.justification: The benchmark procedures, grading, validation, monitoring tools, and scaffold modifications are unchanged, including the implementation descriptions in Appendix A.6.

E1.justification: The same 75 competitions and task domains are evaluated, including the obfuscated-description scenario. The competition inventory in Appendix A.7 and Table 8 is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same four models under AIDE and GPT-4o comparisons using MLAB and OpenHands. The revised contextual count of human medal winners does not change the evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Data splits, medal thresholds, evaluation metrics, hardware configurations, time budgets, and contamination-testing procedures remain unchanged in the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: The attempt-scaling, hardware, runtime, familiarity, description-obfuscation, rule-compliance, and plagiarism analyses are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Seed counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Table 2's 16 seeds for o1-preview/AIDE, 36 for GPT-4o/AIDE, and mean-plus-or-minus-standard-error reporting. Figure 5's correlation and p-value are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 2.2 changes the reported number of humans with medals in 75 different Kaggle competitions from two to nine, with an expanded list in footnote 4. All agent scores, rankings, and experimental findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The pass@k expression, scoring definitions, and familiarity definition are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims, including the 75-competition benchmark and o1-preview/AIDE achieving medals in 16.9% of competitions.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 retains the interpretation that the benchmark ceiling represents exceptional cumulative human achievement. Agent-failure explanations, contamination qualifications, and Section 6's limitations are unchanged; the revised human count adds no separate interpretation.

D1.justification: Hardware, scaffold hyperparameters, prompts, dataset-processing instructions, and code-availability statements are unchanged, including Table 7 and Appendices A.5-A.8.

R1.justification: Footnote 4 replaces Kaggle Rankings with Meta Kaggle as the cited source for the human-medal statistic. This is a limited source-citation change; Section 5, the bibliography, and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is confined to the human-medal sentence, its expanded footnote, and the arXiv version/date stamp. Section organization and the broader narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer footnote causes slight spacing and vertical-placement changes on page 4, including Table 1. No figures or tables are added, removed, redesigned, or reorganized.

improvement.justification: Section 2.2 updates the human-medal count from two to nine and supplies the corresponding names and a revised, dated source. This modestly improves the supporting context for benchmark difficulty. The methodology, experimental evidence, appendices, and main conclusions are unchanged.
